title: EMR: managed Spark and Hadoop, and when it beats Glue

videos.script: Lesson 17 ran a Spark job on Glue and never showed you a machine. EMR shows you all of them. {{cluster}} An EMR cluster is a set of EC2 machines in your account, with Spark and Hadoop already installed. Each machine has a role. The primary node coordinates, core nodes work and store, and task nodes only work. {{roles}} That difference decides which machines may be Spot, the spare capacity AWS sells cheaply and can take back. {{spot}} Work reaches a cluster as steps. A cluster can live for one night and end with its last step, or run all day and wait. {{steps}} moto records every cluster and every step. It runs no Spark, so a step stays running forever, and you will see exactly where that shows. {{moto}} Then the money. Per hour, a machine on EMR costs a little over half of the same capacity on Glue. Left running all month for a two hour job, it costs twelve times what it needed to. {{chart}} By the end you will know when EMR beats Glue, and when it only looks cheaper. {{end}}
